title: US June 2026 Monthly Deficit
question: What will the U.S. Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement first print report for the June 2026 total federal budget deficit or surplus, measured as outlays minus receipts, with deficits positive and surpluses negative?
resolutionSource: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, Monthly Treasury Statement for June 2026
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Monthly Treasury Statement print for June 2026, using total federal outlays minus total federal receipts from the Summary of Receipts, Outlays, and the Deficit/Surplus. Record in USD millions at the agency's published precision. If Treasury labels the month as a surplus, record a negative deficit. Ignore later revisions or annual Combined Statement updates.
drivers: June estimated-tax receipts usually improve the monthly balance
Tariff/customs receipts were elevated in June 2025 and may remain a partial offset
Net interest and mandatory spending keep the deficit baseline high
Calendar timing of benefit payments can move tens of billions between months
Tax legislation and enforcement changes add uncertainty to receipts

reasoning.text: Base rate: June is a high-receipt month because estimated individual and corporate tax payments arrive, so June deficits are usually smaller than adjacent months and can become surpluses. The last two June anchors point to a range from a $66 billion deficit in 2024 to a $27 billion surplus in 2025.

Counter-consideration: the 2025 June surplus had unusually favorable ingredients, including a large spending drop and sharply higher customs receipts. By June 2026, higher interest costs and normalized agency spending could pull the month back into deficit even if tariff revenue remains elevated.

I start from the midpoint of the June 2024 deficit (+66,000 million) and June 2025 surplus (-27,000 million), about +19,500 million. I add roughly +25,000 million for higher net interest and spending normalization, yielding a rounded point of +45,000 million. An 80% interval of -80,000 to +190,000 million allows for tax-payment timing, benefit-payment shifts, and tariff-receipt uncertainty.
